page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Intel Xeon 8163 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded gzip compression, fall into the weak to poor categories, reflecting the older CPU architecture. However, multi-core performance, including Geekbench multi-core, stress-ng multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, reaches average tiers. Memory bandwidth and database operations also perform in the middle 50% range.

Due to the weak single-threaded performance, this instance is not optimal for single-core intensive tasks or latency-sensitive applications. However, the 32 dedicated cores and 128.0 GB of RAM provide average multi-threaded capacity, making it suitable for balanced workloads such as multi-threaded database operations, static web serving, and moderate parallel processing tasks that do not require high single-core clock speeds.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this KVM-hypervised instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Network performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps. Performance benchmarks reveal a significant tradeoff: single-core capabilities are weak, while multi-core execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations consistently achieve average marks. Consequently, this instance is best suited for multi-threaded workloads, static web serving, and general-purpose applications that leverage parallel processing rather than high single-threaded clock speeds.
